Points Through the Steps of Snyder's Projection

Source: R/construction.R
projection_stages.Rd

Snyder's equal-area projection of a face is Lambert's azimuthal equal-area projection about the face's centre, adjusted to fill the face's plane triangle. Lambert's projection has a construction with compass and ruler, and this function returns each point at every step of it, on one face.

Usage

projection_stages(x, lon, lat, face = NULL)

Arguments

x

A HexGridInfo object from hex_grid with Snyder's projection (projection = "isea").

lon, lat

Longitudes and latitudes in degrees (geodetic on the grid's ellipsoid, if it has one: the construction starts from the point's place on the authalic sphere).

face

NULL to take each point onto the face it lies on, or face numbers from 0, one or one per point; the face's formulas are then applied as they stand to points off it.

Value

A data frame with one row per point: lon, lat, face (from 0); arc, \(z\) in degrees; az (\(Az\)) and az_prime (\(Az'\)) in degrees from the face's first vertex, clockwise seen from outside the sphere; Snyder's factor f; the plane coordinates sphere_u, sphere_v, lambert_u, lambert_v, nudge_u, nudge_v, snyder_u, snyder_v; and tx, ty, Snyder's point in triangle coordinates (a face edge is 1). The attribute "r1" holds \(R'\).

Details

With \(T\) the face centre on the sphere and \(S\) a point at arc \(z\) from it and azimuth \(Az\):

sphere

\(S\) itself.

lambert

\(S\) swings about \(T\), in the plane of \(S\) and the normal at \(T\), down onto the tangent plane at \(T\), keeping its distance \(|TS| = 2 \sin(z / 2)\): the Lambert point \(L\), at azimuth \(Az\). This map is equal-area and takes the spherical face to a triangle with curved edges.

nudge

Within the tangent plane, Snyder's adjustment moves \(L\) to azimuth \(Az'\) and radius \(2 f \sin(z / 2)\), which fill each of the face's six right triangles in the plane with area in proportion (Snyder 1992, eqs. 6-11).

snyder

The tangent plane scales by \(R'\) about the sphere's centre onto the face plane, at distance \(R'\) from it; the point lands on Snyder's point \(P\), at radius \(2 R' f \sin(z / 2)\), and the face on the plane triangle of the face's area.

Plane coordinates (u, v) run from the face centre along the x and y axes of the face's plane triangle, the axes of tx and ty, in units of the sphere's radius; an azimuth \(a\) lies along \((\sin a, \cos a)\). Seen from the sphere's centre the planes are parallel, and the point's height along the face's normal is \(\cos z\) for \(S\), 1 on the tangent plane and \(R'\) on the face plane. The sphere point's u and v are its projection onto the planes along the normal.

The scale factors at every step come from projection_distortion with its stage argument; they and these points are computed by the same code as the forward projection, and tx, ty are those hexify_forward returns.

References

Snyder, J. P. (1992). An equal-area map projection for polyhedral globes. Cartographica 29(1), 10-21. doi:10.3138/27H7-8K88-4882-1752

See also

projection_distortion; hex_globe with lambert to follow the construction on a globe

Examples

g <- hex_grid(resolution = 3, aperture = 3)
s <- projection_stages(g, c(0, 10, 16.37), c(40, 45, 48.21))
s

# The Lambert point keeps its distance from the face centre
cbind(lambert = sqrt(s$lambert_u^2 + s$lambert_v^2),
      chord = 2 * sin(s$arc * pi / 360))
